newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Rains halt soy/sugar loading at Brazil's Paranagua.
newsitem.headline: Rains halt soy/sugar loading at Brazil's Paranagua.

text.p: Heavy rains interrupted loading of sugar and soy exports at Brazil's port of Paranagua, a port authority spokeswoman said.
"It's been raining since 0600 (local/0900 GMT). People are just waiting for it to stop before starting again," she added.
In the port of Santos, light rains have not affected operations so far, a port authority spokesman said.
Both ports reported the following conditions for shipping soybeans, soy products and sugar:

Vessels: Azalea Estrella loading 36,750 soybeans, Angelic Protector loading 57,040 tonnes soybeans, Cornilios loading 50,255 tonnes soymeal, Andromachi loading soybeans/soymeal Waiting to dock: one vessel to load soybeans, 9 to load soymeal and three to load mixed soybeans/soymeal
Road: 962 trucks carrying soybeans arrived on May 13, 312 trucks with soymeal and 115 trucks with vegetable oils including soyoil
SANTOS - SUGAR Docked: none Waiting to dock: two waiting to load 28,000 tonnes bagged sugar
